paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea: God's mercy comes first, and your whole life answers it. Paul says, "Therefore I urge you, brothers, on account of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as living sacrifices, holy and pleasing to God, which is your spiritual service of worship." (Romans 12:1) Worship isn't just a song on a Sunday. It's your body, your Monday, your whole ordinary day handed over to Him.

That's why Paul says, "Do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind." (Romans 12:2) The world is a loud stamper, baker, and it wants to press you into ITS shape every single day. God doesn't press you from the outside. He renews you from the inside, so you can test and approve His will, which Paul calls "the good, pleasing, and perfect will of God." (Romans 12:2) And I still can't get over it: God's will is good, pleasing AND perfect, and I've never had a batch come out all three!

Then Paul brings it home to the church. Don't think of yourself more highly than you ought, but think with sober judgment, because "in Christ we who are many are one body, and each member belongs to one another." (Romans 12:3, 5) Your gift isn't for bragging and it isn't for hiding. God gave it to you so you can serve the whole body, so go and use it, friend!
